about: Readiness meters. Each item counts only when it is merged on main with evidence. done = full weight, partial = half, not-started = none. Edit this file, then run `python3 scripts/readiness.py` to regenerate the badges and the README table; CI runs `--check`. Evidence: {"pr": N} (squash-merged on main), {"path": "repo/relative"} (must exist), {"test": "name", "path": "file"} (file must contain the name). `tracking` names the open PR or issue for work not yet done.

meters.title: OS strength
meters.summary: MedBrains OS: the hospital appliance's security, updates and recovery.

items.title: A bootable OS image built from source, checked by tests that boot it
Default-deny firewall, authenticated time and first Linux hardening
Data disk encrypted, with every key accounted for
Signed A/B updates with trial boots and rollback; tampered and rolled-back updates refused
Built-in identity provider (Kanidm); the first administrator enrols an authenticator at setup
A machine joins the main machine only by approval, over encrypted links
Memory-safe front proxy (Pingora) in place of Caddy
Append-only, hash-chained audit log of every change and record opened
Backups sealed to an offline key, with a restore drill that proves they restore
Wipe an OS machine's data disk, restore it and verify (ransomware test)
Sealed, read-only system partition (dm-verity)
Kernel, service sandbox and AppArmor hardening, scored against CIS
Release signing keys kept offline before the update feed opens
Secure Boot with our own key and a signed boot image
Room to grow on the system partition (8 MB left today)
Release shipped as an installer ISO, VM and cloud disks
Tests passed on real hardware, not only virtual machines
External penetration test report

meters.title: Paperless
meters.summary: Paperless records: signed, verifiable clinical records instead of paper files.

items.title: One case sheet per visit: written, signed and filed to the medical record
Medical records custodian: opens every chart, each opening logged
Signed prints carry a QR that lets an outsider check the record is unchanged; signing needs a fresh step-up
A meter of how paperless the hospital is, by department and day
Every clinical record type signable by its author (21 types); partial because signing keys still sit on the server
Each doctor signs with their own hardware key (badge or FIDO2); the server cannot sign as them
Legal electronic signatures (remote DSC, eSign) through providers
Patient e-consent with capacity, witness and separate purposes
One-click court certificate from the seal chain and audit log
Transfer to another hospital with signatures kept and checkable
Downtime mode: a read-only snapshot and offline entry when the server is down
Connector that runs beside another hospital system (HL7 and FHIR in)

meters.title: AI clinical flows
meters.summary: AI that drafts clinical work for a clinician to review, on the hospital's own machines.

items.title: Doctor records or uploads dictation; it becomes note sections and medicines, each reviewed before saving

evidence.test: saves only accepted (and edited) sections into the note, and hands accepted medicines to the pad

items.title: Every model call goes through one pseudonymising redaction layer
Every AI answer is labelled, and reaches a record only when a clinician accepts it (audited)
Dictated medicines become a prescription only through the allergy, interaction and dose checks
Local speech and language models shipped as an OS service on the appliance
Kernel AI interface with permissions, consent and audit on every call
MCP server so outside assistants work under the same permissions
Voice capture in the native iOS and Android apps
Speech in local languages and mixed-language dictation
Patient consent captured before a consultation is recorded
Dictation that works with no network

meters.title: HIPAA readiness
meters.summary: US HIPAA Security, Privacy and Breach Notification Rules, as they apply to the software. Not a certification: none exists for HIPAA.

items.title: Unique user identification: one login per person, unique within the hospital (164.312(a)(2)(i))
Emergency access: break the glass with a reason, reviewed afterwards (164.312(a)(2)(ii))
Automatic logoff after inactivity (164.312(a)(2)(iii)); today a 7-day refresh token keeps an idle session alive
Encryption at rest (164.312(a)(2)(iv)); partial because only the OS appliance encrypts its own disk, other installs rely on the host
Audit controls: append-only, hash-chained log of changes, refusals and failed sign-ins (164.312(b))
Integrity: signed records an outsider can check are unchanged (164.312(c))
Person authentication: TOTP second factor and a fresh step-up before signing (164.312(d))
Transmission security: TLS at the front and between database nodes (164.312(e))
Minimum necessary access: role permissions plus per-patient checks; partial until every module passes the authorization ledger
Contingency plan: sealed backups with a restore drill (164.308(a)(7))
Patient right of access: a copy of their record, downloadable from the portal (164.524)
Accounting of disclosures (164.528); partial: who opened the record and which insurers received it, not every disclosure
Breach notification within 60 days (164.404-410); partial: a breach register with clocks, but for the DPDP and CERT-In deadlines, not HIPAA's
Security risk analysis (164.308(a)(1)); partial: an OS threat model, no HIPAA risk analysis
Business associate agreement template for hosted installs (164.308(b))

meters.title: GDPR readiness
meters.summary: EU GDPR duties a hospital system has to support. Much of the evidence is shared with DPDP; EU-specific parts are mostly open.

items.title: Lawful basis per purpose for health data (Art. 6, 9); partial: consent per purpose and care as a legitimate use, not an Art. 9(2) basis per processing
Transparent notice at collection (Art. 13); partial: a versioned notice in English, Hindi and Tamil, none in EU languages
Withdraw consent as easily as giving it, by the patient (Art. 7(3))
Right of access: what the hospital holds and who received it (Art. 15)
Rectification, erasure and restriction (Art. 16-18); partial: requests recorded and answered with a reason, changes made by hand, no restriction request
Portability: the patient downloads their record as FHIR (Art. 20)
Breach notice to the authority within 72 hours and to the people affected (Art. 33-34); partial: the clocks name India's Board, not an EU supervisory authority
Processor register with the agreement, data and country of each (Art. 28)
Records of processing activities (Art. 30); partial: processors are registered, the hospital's own processing is not
Data protection officer named and published (Art. 37-39)
Data protection impact assessment record (Art. 35)
International transfers under safeguards (Chapter V); partial: processor countries recorded and AI calls pseudonymised, no transfer mechanism record
Security and privacy by design: encryption, pseudonymisation, audit (Art. 25, 32)

meters.title: DPDP readiness
meters.summary: India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and Rules 2025, for a hospital as Data Fiduciary.

items.title: Itemised notice at registration and consent recorded purpose by purpose (s.5-6, r.3)
Notice in English and any Eighth Schedule language (s.5(3)); partial: Hindi and Tamil only
Withdrawal as easy as consent, by the patient from the portal and apps (s.6(4))
Rights requests (access, correction, erasure, nominee, grievance) answered within 90 days (s.11-14, r.14)
DPO and grievance officer named and published to patients (r.9)
Breach intimation to the Board and each person affected, with the 72-hour report clock (s.8(6), r.7)
Register of processors with their agreement (s.8(2))
Verifiable guardian consent for children and no tracking of them (s.9, r.10); partial: a guardian is named, but age does not force it and marketing does not exclude minors
Erase when the purpose ends, with 48 hours' notice to the person (s.8(7), r.8)
Security safeguards and access logs kept a year (r.6); partial: encryption and the audit log, but log retention differs by install
Consent Manager integration (s.6(7-9), r.4); partial: ABDM consent artefacts are kept, no DPDP Consent Manager
Cross-border transfers only where allowed (s.16); partial: processor countries recorded and AI calls pseudonymised, no transfer log

meters.title: ABDM readiness
meters.summary: India's Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission milestones M1-M3, Scan & Share and NHCX. Built in code; not yet through the ABDM sandbox test or certification.

items.title: M1: create an ABHA by Aadhaar OTP, with the Aadhaar number sent encrypted and never kept
M1: find and verify an ABHA, show its QR and card, link it to the patient
Scan & Share: counter QR, token on profile share, desk queue, on web and the staff app
M2: link each visit's records to the ABHA and share them under consent, Fidelius-encrypted
M3: request and view a patient's records from other hospitals, with consent
NRCeS IG 6.5.0 record bundles passing the official validator; partial: HealthDocument and Invoice records held until the terminology run passes
Gateway callbacks open only with the gateway's token, each hospital seeing only its own
Facility (HFR) and professional (HPR) registry identities
NHCX: eligibility, pre-auth and final claims sent and followed up
Passed the ABDM sandbox functional test for M1-M3
ABDM certification and production keys

meters.title: NABH readiness
meters.summary: Not assessed yet: the NABH hospital and digital-health standards have over a thousand objective elements, and this pass did not map them to evidence.

meters.title: CERT-In readiness
meters.summary: India's CERT-In Directions of 28 April 2022 under the IT Act, s.70B.

items.title: An incident assessed as reportable starts a 6-hour clock from discovery, escalated when overdue (direction ii)
The CERT-In report is recorded once, with its date and reference
Point of contact named (direction vi)
ICT logs kept 180 days in India (direction iv); partial: standalone installs keep 180 days, the OS image keeps 3 months
Clocks synced to NIC or NPL time (direction i); partial: authenticated NTS time, but from other national and public servers
Incident response plan, with breach drills recorded
Security audit by a CERT-In empanelled auditor

meters.title: EU CRA readiness
meters.summary: EU Cyber Resilience Act essential requirements (Annex I) and vulnerability handling, for MedBrains as a product with digital elements.

items.title: Software bill of materials for every build (Annex I part II(1))
Coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy and a published contact (Annex I part II(5-6))
No known exploitable vulnerabilities: locked builds and dependency audits as gates (Annex I part I(2)(a))
Security updates signed, with rollback, and tampered updates refused (Annex I part I(2)(c))
Support period declared (Art. 13(8))
Secure by default configuration (Annex I part I(2)(b)): default-deny firewall, integrations off without their keys
Limit attack surface (Annex I part I(2)(j)); partial: kernel and service hardening merged, CIS scoring open
Confidentiality and integrity of stored data (Annex I part I(2)(e-f))
Cybersecurity risk assessment in the technical file (Art. 13(2-3)); partial: a threat model for the OS only
Report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents within 24 hours (Art. 14)
Conformity assessment, EU declaration of conformity and CE marking (Art. 28-32)

meters.title: EHDS readiness
meters.summary: Not assessed yet: the European Health Data Space requirements for EHR systems (the European exchange format and the harmonised components) were not mapped to evidence in this pass.

meters.title: FHIR readiness
meters.summary: HL7 FHIR R4 as a server other systems can rely on.

items.title: A CapabilityStatement that says what the server supports
Read core resources; partial: Patient, Encounter, Observation and DiagnosticReport, not Condition, MedicationRequest, AllergyIntolerance or Practitioner
Document bundles (Composition) for case sheets and ABDM records
Bundles gated on the official HL7 validator, and checked again at send time
A patient's whole record as a FHIR bundle ($everything and the portal download)
Coded with SNOMED CT, LOINC and UCUM; partial: membership is proven only by a nightly terminology run not yet seen green
Search interactions on the REST API
Create and update through the REST API
SMART on FHIR authorization for outside apps
Bulk data export ($export)
Conformance to an international profile set (IPS or US Core)

meters.title: Medical device (SaMD) controls
meters.summary: Classification meter: no MedBrains feature is meant to be a regulated medical device. Each item is a control that keeps AI and decision features assistive, so a clinician decides.

items.title: AI text reaches a record only when a clinician accepts, edits or rejects each item

evidence.test: saves only accepted (and edited) sections into the note, and hands accepted medicines to the pad

items.title: Every screen that shows AI output labels it, checked in CI
Every accept, edit or reject is kept as an AI-governance record
AI-suggested medicines become a prescription only through the clinician and the allergy, interaction and dose checks
Intended use written per AI capability; partial: dictation is written down as a documentation aid, not yet signed off by a regulatory adviser
One strict AI component seam (draft cards, flags, never pre-selected, override needs a reason), enforced by a CI check and the server
Claim gate: intended-use statement and risk register before any diagnostic, triage or monitoring claim
Written classification under CDSCO, EU MDR and US FDA before any device-like feature is built
